title: Which Bible Figure Hid Their Wound Like You Do?
subtitle: After we get hurt, we all build some kind of armor. Let's name yours, and see how God came looking anyway.

questions.text: After you got hurt, what did you do?

options.text: I ran. I put distance between myself and everyone.
I hid somewhere small, convinced I was worthless.
I fled into the wilderness of my own mind, alone.
I disappeared in shame over how I had failed.

questions.text: What does your armor sound like on the inside?

options.text: I cannot do this anymore. I just want to be left alone.
Why would anyone want me? I am nothing.
No one sees me out here, and no one is coming.
I blew it. I cannot face anyone now.

questions.text: How do you keep people from getting close to the wound?

options.text: I isolate and tell myself I am better off alone.
I stay out of sight so no one can reject me first.
I wander off emotionally before anyone can leave me.
I avoid the people who knew me before I failed.

questions.text: Which feeling drives you into hiding?

options.text: Exhaustion, like I have nothing left to give.
Shame that I am damaged and unwanted.
The ache of feeling completely overlooked.
Guilt over the moment I let someone down.

questions.text: How has the wound changed how you see yourself?

options.text: I feel done, like I have already given my best and failed.
I see myself as the broken one no one would choose.
I feel invisible, like I do not matter to anyone.
I have come home empty, and even my name feels bitter now.

questions.text: If someone reached toward you right now, what would you do?

options.text: Pull further into my cave. I am not ready to be found.
Brace for them to realize I am not worth the trouble.
Wonder if they actually see me, or just feel sorry for me.
Look away, sure they remember how I failed.

questions.text: What do you secretly long for in your hiding place?

options.text: Rest, and a gentle voice that does not demand more of me.
A seat at a table I never thought I belonged at.
To be truly seen by someone who knows my name.
A second chance from the One I let down.

questions.text: How is your faith doing in the hiding?

options.text: Burned out. I am too tired to even pray much.
Quiet. I assume God overlooks me like everyone else.
Lonely. I am not sure God remembers I am out here.
Heavy with regret, unsure if I can be restored.

questions.text: What would mean the most coming from God right now?

options.text: Gentle care first, before He asks anything of me.
You belong at my table, just as you are.
I see you. I have seen you this whole time.
I am not finished with you. Come back.

elijah.name: Elijah (Ran and Isolated in the Cave)
elijah.description: When the weight got to be too much, you ran and pulled into a cave where no one could reach you. Elijah did the same: burned out, wanting to disappear, certain he was finished. But God did not scold him. He came near, fed him, let him rest, and only then spoke in a gentle whisper. That same tenderness is coming toward you. He is not asking you to perform. He just wants to care for you first.

scripture.text: And, behold, the Lord passed by ... and after the fire a still small voice.

mephibosheth.name: Mephibosheth (Hid in Lo-Debar, Sure He Was Worthless)
mephibosheth.description: You have tucked yourself away in some Lo-Debar of your own, convinced you are too broken to be wanted. Mephibosheth lived there too, hiding and calling himself as good as dead. But the king sought him out, not to shame him, but to seat him at the royal table as family for the rest of his days. God is doing the same for you. He is not looking for the polished version. He wants you at His table exactly as you are.

scripture.text: Thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

hagar.name: Hagar (Fled to the Wilderness)
hagar.description: When you felt cast aside, you fled into a wilderness where you were sure no one would notice you were gone. Hagar ran there too, alone and invisible. But God met her in that empty place, and she gave Him a name: the God who sees me. You are not overlooked, no matter how forgotten you feel. The same God found Hagar in the desert, and He sees you right where you are hiding.

peter.name: Peter (Hid in Shame After Denying Jesus)
peter.description: You are hiding behind shame over a moment you failed, sure you have disqualified yourself. Peter knew that exact weight after he denied Jesus three times and wept bitterly. But Jesus came looking for him, made him breakfast, and gently restored him three times over. Your failure is not the end of your story. The One you let down is not finished with you. He is coming to restore you, not to shame you.

scripture.text: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? ... Feed my sheep.

naomi.name: Naomi (Came Home Empty and Renamed Herself Bitter)
naomi.description: You came home from your loss feeling so hollow that even your old name no longer fit, so bitterness took its place. Naomi felt it too. She told people to call her Mara, which means bitter. But her story did not end in that emptiness. God was quietly working a redemption she could not yet see, and joy found its way back to her. Your bitterness is not the final chapter, and the God who restored Naomi can restore you too.

scripture.text: Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.
